transcript: She is not simply tired, she is carrying too much. Her nervous system has been awake for a long time, longer than the body was meant to stay alert. She has been walking a long path with no clear end in sight. Even the studies of the modern world say this. Motherhood can place more strain on the body and mind than the highest pressure work of men in tall buildings. Why? Because work allows pauses. Motherhood does not. She is always listening. Even in sleep, her spirit stays alert. A breath, a sound, a cry. Her body responds before her mind wakes. She is not exhausted because she is weak. She is exhausted because she never stops holding. Her mind is always moving. Did they eat enough? What comes next? Did I forget something? Am I doing enough? The room may look quiet, but inside her body there is no silence. Her nervous system believes it must stay ready, as if danger could arrive at any moment. So when you see a mother staring into space, moving slowly or speaking sharply, do not judge her. Understand this, she has been holding the weight of many lives with a body that is asking, softly, for rest. If this felt like it was speaking from inside your body, then your nervous system is asking for help. The way back to stillness was written for this exact state, for the woman who has been holding everything together while forgetting how to rest herself. You don't need motivation. You need safety. The way back is waiting. Link in my profile.
